correctness.rationale: Each ordered triple of four-letter center words yields exactly one equality partition of twelve labeled letter positions, canonically encoded as a restricted-growth sequence, and conversely every such partition plus an injective q-symbol relabeling yields all triples realizing that pattern. The partitions are a finite exhaustive domain of size B_12=4,213,597, independent of q. Excluding equal four-position blocks leaves 4,201,207 admissible ordered-center patterns. For each pattern, the 6 surviving index pairs per center are represented as ordered-pair bitsets; the intersection of all three bitsets counts distinct common two-letter outputs exactly, with duplicate outputs collapsed. An independent C++ enumerator written separately from the package visited all 4,213,597 patterns, reproduced all 4,201,207 admissible patterns, all 28 displayed coefficient cells (including zeros) and all no-overlap cells, and confirmed maximum 4. A pattern with k classes contributes exactly (q)_k alphabet injective assignments; each unordered triple is counted six times, proving the all-q polynomial identities rather than extrapolating q=2,3,4,5. Witness (0101,0110,1001) has all four possible binary pairs in the intersection, while the table has no k>4 contribution at maximum. The original direct q=2..5 table and first-moment identity were also checked for consistency.

value.rationale: This is the first admissible n=t+ℓ−1 boundary for the three-center two-deletion extension highlighted in a primary paper. The complete alphabet-dependent overlap spectrum and exact rarity of worst-case triples quantify natural ambiguity patterns, including the four-letter/DNA alphabet, beyond a bare known binary maximum. The exhaustive 12-position equality-pattern method proves a natural exact finite structural classification for all q; no claim of general code-rate gains or arbitrary n is made.
